notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't write these notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

My first attempt went straight to the commentary pages, but the fetch tool rejected every address. It only opens pages that have first turned up in a search, and I hadn't searched yet. When I then tried to run those searches, the system said I had no research calls left for this turn. So I haven't read Enduring Word, Bible Hub, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes or any of the other sites.

Your rule is to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. I didn't want to break that by writing notes from memory without real links, so there are no verse notes here.

If you send the request again, or just say "continue," I'll start with searches so the pages can be opened. Here's the plan:

1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word, plus Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill on Bible Hub or StudyLight, and Precept Austin, read verse by verse.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** each tradition's own sites on three passages:
   - v. 4 and vv. 9–11, trusting the temple and the "den of robbers" (which Jesus quotes in Matthew 21:13)
   - v. 16, the command not to pray for the people
   - vv. 21–23, the debated line that God did not command sacrifices
3. **Other views:** NET Bible and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, the Catholic and Orthodox sites on the Queen of Heaven (v. 18) and on Topheth and Gehenna (vv. 31–32), and the sites' own discussion of prosperity or hyper-grace teaching on false assurance (v. 10), if they have any.

Each point will have its URL, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
